page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v3 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance belonging to the ESv3 family. Built on x86_64 architecture and virtualized with Microsoft Hyper-V, this server features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores operating at 2.6 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system provides 64.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation ratio. Hardware specifications include 131 GB of local SSD storage alongside Premium Storage capability, a 50 MB L3 cache, and x86 vector extensions including AVX and AVX-512F.

Benchmark evaluation demonstrates balanced memory performance alongside modest raw CPU processing capabilities. Memory bandwidth testing records 365.1 GB/sec for small-block cached reads and 42.29 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, with a PassMark memory score of 2294.36. In database and caching workloads, the server achieves 6.16 million Redis SET operations per second and average PassMark database operation scores. Single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores, place general compute throughput in the bottom 25% quartile. Small 135M model LLM text generation reaches 102.6 tokens per second, whereas 7B model inference yields 5.03 tokens per second.

The E8s_v3 delivers strong resource density for memory-bound applications where raw processing speed is secondary. Provisioning 8 GB of memory per vCPU makes this configuration effective for running database buffers and caching layers. The integrated 131 GB local SSD storage provides fast temporary storage for system swap and transient operational data. Primary target workloads include relational database management systems, key-value caches like Redis, software compilation pipelines, and enterprise application backends requiring high memory capacity.
